arxiv-1910-01487.title: Generalization Bounds for Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-1910-01487.creator: Shan Lin slin4492@uni.sydney.edu.au, Jingwei Zhang zjin8228@uni.sydney.edu.au
arxiv-1910-01487.description: Abstract Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved breakthrough performances in a wide range of applications including image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection. Previous research on characterizing the generalization ability of neural networks mostly focuses on fully connected neural networks (FNNs), regarding CNNs as a special case of FNNs without taking into account the special structure of convolutional layers.

arxiv-2102-10157.title: Self-organized vortex and antivortex patterns in laser arrays
arxiv-2102-10157.creator: M. Honari-Latifpour, J. Ding, S. Takei, M.-A. Miri
arxiv-2102-10157.description: Abstract Recently it is shown that dissipatively coupled laser arrays simulate the classical XY model. We show that phase-locking of laser arrays can give rise to the spontaneous formation of vortex and antivortex phase patterns that are analogous to topological defects of the XY model.

arxiv-2201-11015.title: INTERSECTION DENSITY OF TRANSITIVE GROUPS WITH CYCLIC POINT STABILIZERS
arxiv-2201-11015.description: Abstract For a permutation group G G acting on a set V V , a subset ℱ \mathcal{F} of G G is said to be an intersecting set if for every pair of elements g , h ∈ ℱ g,h\in\mathcal{F} there exists v ∈ V v\in V such that g ⁡ ( v ) = h ⁡ ( v )

arxiv-2206-06830.title: Mixed-Mode Chimera States in Pendula Networks
arxiv-2206-06830.creator: P. Ebrahimzadeh, M. Schiek, Y. Maistrenko
arxiv-2206-06830.description: Abstract We report the emergence of peculiar chimera states in networks of identical pendula with global phase-lagged coupling. The states reported include both rotating and quiescent modes, i.e. with non-zero and zero average frequencies. This kind mixed-mode chimeras may be interpreted as images of bump states known in neuroscience in the context of modelling the working memory.

arxiv-2212-12555.title: Low-temperature thermal corrections to a superfluid’s equation of state
arxiv-2212-12555.creator: Ioanna Kourkoulou, Alberto Nicolis, Klaas Parmentier
arxiv-2212-12555.description: Abstract Using effective field theory methods, we calculate the low-temperature phonon thermal partition function for a generic superfluid, thus providing the leading thermal corrections to a superfluid’s equation of state, thermodynamic quantities, and conserved currents. We confirm the correctness of the classic two-fluid model by matching to the effective field theory for that model.

arxiv-2305-06960.title: A Fixed–Point Approach to Non–Commutative Central Limit Theorems
arxiv-2305-06960.creator: Jad Hamdan
arxiv-2305-06960.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jad Hamdan. We show how the renormalization group approach can be used to prove quantitative central limit theorems (CLTs) in the setting of free, Boolean, bi–free and bi–Boolean independence under finite third moment assumptions. The proofs rely on the construction of a contractive metric over the space of probability measures over ℝ \mathbb{R} or ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , which has the appropriate analogue of a Gaussian distribution as a fixed point (for instance, the semi–circle law in the case of free independence).

arxiv-2407-08400.title: Self-training Language Models for Arithmetic Reasoning
arxiv-2407-08400.creator: Marek Kadlčík, Michal Štefánik Faculty of Informatics, Masaryk University, Czech Republic {kadlcik,stefanik.m}@mail.muni.cz
arxiv-2407-08400.description: Abstract Recent language models achieve impressive results in tasks involving complex multistep reasoning, but scaling these capabilities further traditionally requires expensive collection of more annotated data. In this work, we explore the potential of improving models’ reasoning capabilities without new data, merely using automated feedback to the validity of their predictions in arithmetic reasoning ( self-training ).

arxiv-2410-07481.title: Effects of dissipation in reservoir computing using spin qubit array
arxiv-2410-07481.creator: Shion Mifune, Taro Kanao, Tetsufumi Tanamoto
arxiv-2410-07481.description: Abstract Reservoir computing (RC) is one of the hottest topics as a promising application for many physical devices because their device characteristics can be directly used in the computing sequences. Quantum RC is also the promising candidate for the application of even small-number qubit system.

arxiv-2509-18406.title: A constrained iteratively reweighted least squares framework for generalised linear models
arxiv-2509-18406.creator: Pierre Masselot, Devon Nenon, Jacopo Vanoli, Zaid Chalabi, Antonio Gasparrini
arxiv-2509-18406.description: Abstract Many applications of generalised linear models (GLMs) can be improved by applying constraints that impose assumptions on the associations and improve consistency of the estimators. Yet, there are still barriers to the implementation and practical application of constrained GLMs.

arxiv-2510-06498.title: Non-Gaussian states via pump-depleted SPDC
arxiv-2510-06498.creator: Colin Vendromin, Samuel E. Fontaine, J. E. Sipe
arxiv-2510-06498.description: Abstract We develop a model for non-Gaussian state generation via spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in InGaP microring resonators. The nonlinear Hamiltonian is written in terms of the asymptotic fields for the system, which includes a phantom channel to handle scattering loss.

arxiv-2601-07892.title: Sherry: Hardware-Efficient 1.25-Bit Ternary Quantization via Fine-grained Sparsification
arxiv-2601-07892.creator: Hong Huang Decheng Wu Qiangqiang Hu Guanghua Yu Jinhai Yang, Jianchen Zhu Xue Liu Dapeng Wu
arxiv-2601-07892.description: Abstract The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained edge devices is increasingly hindered by prohibitive memory and computational requirements. While ternary quantization offers a compelling solution by reducing weights to { − 1 , 0 , + 1 } \{-1,0,+1\} , current implementations suffer from a fundamental misalignment with commodity hardware.

arxiv-2602-12206.title: Making the complete OpenAIRE citation graph easily accessible through compact data representation
arxiv-2602-12206.creator: Joakim Skarding, Pavel Sanda
arxiv-2602-12206.description: Abstract The OpenAIRE graph contains a large citation graph dataset, with over 200 million publications and over 2 billion citations. The current graph is available as a dump with metadata which uncompressed totals ∼ 2.5 \sim 2.5 TB. This makes it hard to process on conventional computers.

arxiv-2604-05679.title: Asymptotic models for viscoelastic one-dimensional blood flow
arxiv-2604-05679.creator: Diego Alonso-Orán, Rafael Granero-Belinchón, Carlos Yanes Pérez

britannica-1911-stanislaus-ii-augustus.title: Stanislaus II. Augustus (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-stanislaus-ii-augustus.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-stanislaus-ii-augustus.description: Article 'Stanislaus II. Augustus' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. king of Poland, the son of Stanislaw Poniatowski, palatine of Cracow, the friend and companion of Charles XII. Born in 1732 he owed his advance in life to the influence of his uncles the powerful Czartoryscy, who sent him to St Petersburg in the suite of the English ambassador Hanbury Williams.

pmc-10506903.title: Self-Esteem Trajectories After Occupational Injuries and Diseases and Their Relation to Changes in Subjective Health: Result From the Panel Study of Workers’ Compensation Insurance (PSWCI)
pmc-10506903.creator: Seong-Uk Baek, Won-Tae Lee, Min-Seok Kim, Myeong-Hun Lim, Jin-Ha Yoon, Jong-Uk Won
pmc-10506903.description: BackgroundOccupational injuries and diseases are life events that significantly impact an individuals’ identity. In this study, we examined the trajectories of self-esteem among victims of occupational injury and disease and their relation to health.MethodsThe Panel Study of Workers’ Compensation Insurance conducted annual follow-ups on workers who had experienced occupational injury or disease.

pmc-11539683.title: Identifying low-density, ancestry-informative SNP markers through whole genome resequencing in Indian, Chinese, and wild yak
pmc-11539683.creator: Munish Gangwar, Sheikh Firdous Ahmad, Abdul Basit Ali, Amit Kumar, Amod Kumar, Gyanendra Kumar Gaur, Triveni Dutt
pmc-11539683.description: The current investigation was undertaken to elucidate the population-stratifying and ancestry-informative markers in Indian, Chinese, and wild yak populations using whole genome resequencing (WGS) analysis while employing various selection strategies (Delta, Pairwise Wright’s Fixation Index-FST, and Informativeness of Assignment) and marker densities (5–25 thousand). The study used WGS data on 105 individuals from three separate yak cohorts i.e.

pmc-11709897.title: Advanced modeling of Alzheimer’s disease using human iPSC‐derived microglia and neurons carrying disease‐related mutations
pmc-11709897.creator: Berta Sanz Morello, Elin Byman Shatri, Sofie Frandsen, Benjamin Schmid, Kenneth Thirstrup, Bjørn Holst
pmc-11709897.description: BackgroundMicroglia are the primary immune cells of the brain and represent the main line of defense against brain environmental insults. In recent years, microglia have been implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis by having interconnected yet opposing roles: beneficial as they clear amyloid beta (Aβ) and amyloid plaques, and detrimental as being responsible for synaptic and neuronal loss.

pmc-12362941.title: Comparative effectiveness of antibiotic prophylaxis for preventing serious adverse events after primary total hip arthroplasty: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized trials
pmc-12362941.creator: Armita A ABEDI, Jacob M SVENSSON, Alma B PEDERSEN, Claus VARNUM, Sabrina M NIELSEN, Jens H LAIGAARD, Robin CHRISTENSEN, Søren OVERGAARD
pmc-12362941.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and purposeThe optimal duration of antibiotic prophylaxis for reducing serious adverse events (SAEs) after total hip arthroplasty (THA) is unclear. We aimed to assess the comparative effectiveness of different strategies of antibiotic prophylaxis in preventing SAEs after THA.MethodsWe searched Medline, Embase, CENTRAL, and the Clinical Trial Registration Database for randomized controlled trials evaluating antibiotic prophylaxis in patients undergoing primary THA. Two authors independently screened, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias.

pmc-12497975.title: Predictive Value of Plasma Epstein-Barr Virus DNA Concentration for Recurrence and Metastasis in Advanced-Stage Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Longitudinal, Descriptive Investigation
pmc-12497975.creator: Huong Do Lan, Thuan Nghiem Duc, Ba Nguyen Van, Nam Thanh Quan, Dang Nguyen Van, Tuan Dinh Le, Son Tien Nguyen, Binh Van Nguyen
pmc-12497975.description: Background:Vietnam is an endemic region for nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC), with approximately 70% of cases diagnosed at stage III-IVa and 90% presenting with undifferentiated histology closely related to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection. However, no studies have identified biomarkers predictive of recurrence and metastasis.

pmc-12557864.title: The Healthcare Amyloidosis European Registry (HEAR): design of a national registry with a European extension strategy, and foundation of the F-CRIN GRACE network
pmc-12557864.creator: Patricia Réant, Mounira Kharoubi, Erwan Donal, Fabrice Bauer, Mélanie Bézard, Arnaud Bisson, Diane Bodez, Océane Bouchot, Eve Cariou, Phillipe Charron, Jérôme Costa, Pierre-Yves Courand, Charlotte Dagrenat, Francois Delelis, Antoine Jobbe Duval, Jean-Christophe Eicher, Antoine Fraix, Barnabas Gellen
pmc-12557864.description: BackgroundCardiac amyloidosis (CA) is a rare disease that can lead to poor quality of life, conduction disorders, arrhythmia, heart failure, and even death. Fortunately, specific treatments that can modify the natural history of the disease and the disease outcomes are now available. However, data on the prevailing patient management procedures and long-term outcomes of CA are scarce.

pmc-12565641.title: Recent Advances in Secondary Metabolites from Marine Aspergillus
pmc-12565641.creator: Zimin Wang, Meirong Zhao, Chenglin Li, Yunxia Yu, Zhiqiang Gong, Fandong Kong, Chengzhi Li
pmc-12565641.description: Marine Aspergillus fungi, adapted to extreme marine environments (e.g., sediments, corals, mangroves), are prolific producers of structurally diverse secondary metabolites with significant bioactivities. This review comprehensively analyzes 340 novel natural products reported from 81 marine-derived Aspergillus strains over the past three years, classifying them into six major categories: alkaloids (31.2%), polyketides (29.4%), terpenoids, lignans, cyclopeptides, and others.

pmc-13144216.title: Outcomes of early versus late radiotherapy in grade 2 meningiomas: a National retrospective analysis from the TROD neuro-oncology group
pmc-13144216.creator: Volkan Demircan, Ertuğrul Şentürk, Evrim Tezcanlı, Petek Erpolat, Züleyha Akgün, Serra Kamer, Necla Gürdal, Beyhan Ceylaner Bıçakçı, Burak Erdemci, Nuri Kaydıhan, Banu Atalar
pmc-13144216.description: PurposeThe optimal timing of radiotherapy (RT) in patients with WHO grade 2 meningiomas remains controversial, particularly following gross total resection (GTR). This multicenter study compared long-term outcomes of early RT versus late RT, focusing on progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and tumor-related mortality.

pmc-13281896.title: Subgroup-Specific Nomogram for Refined Risk Stratification in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Patients with Low LDL-C
pmc-13281896.creator: Bojun Liu, Zhixia Gu, Ling Li, Lei Li, Ronghua Jin, Caixia Hu

pmc-13289579.title: Differential Causal Associations of Gut Microbiota, Blood Metabolites, and Immune Cell Phenotypes With Early- and Late-Onset Alzheimer’s Disease: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Analysis
pmc-13289579.creator: Yuejun Wang, LIfang Wang, Dehua Zhan
pmc-13289579.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a heterogeneous syndrome with distinct genetic and clinical profiles between early-onset AD (EOAD) and late-onset AD (LOAD) subtypes. However, specific causal etiologies linking the gut microbiota-immune-metabolic axis to these subtypes remain poorly understood.Methods: We employed a comprehensive bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) framework to systematically investigate the causal associations of gut microbiota, immune cell phenotypes, and blood metabolites with EOAD and LOAD.

pmc-13337704.title: Early aortic valve intervention versus clinical surveillance in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13337704.creator: Umar G. Adamu, Confidence Makgoro, El-ameen U. Adamu, David Mashilo, Anupa Patel, Nqoba Tsabedze

pmc-13344621.title: Redefining fetal growth restriction using gastroschisis‐specific growth curves
pmc-13344621.creator: Rebecca Simon, Elissa Moody, Rosemary Shay, Brittany Bergam, Ronit Katz, Shani Delaney
pmc-13344621.description: IntroductionFetal growth restriction (FGR) occurs in a significant proportion of pregnancies complicated by gastroschisis. Due to abdominal organ herniation, fetal abdominal circumference often measures less than expected when using Hadlock biometric measurements derived from non‐anomalous fetuses. Therefore, growth restriction may be overdiagnosed in fetuses with gastroschisis.

pmc-13473554.title: Blood glucose trajectory phenotypes are associated with in-hospital mortality in a multicenter ICU stroke cohort
pmc-13473554.creator: Juan Wang, Hai-Bo Li, Wen-Juan Li, Man-Man Xu, Chun-Hua Hang, Peng-Lai Zhao
pmc-13473554.description: Non-traumatic stroke (NTS) is associated with high mortality, and dynamic glucose patterns may provide prognostic information beyond static glucose measurements. This study aimed to identify glucose trajectory phenotypes in ICU patients with NTS and evaluate their association with in-hospital mortality. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included ICU patients with NTS from MIMIC-IV, eICU, and NSICU.

pmc-13654155.title: Interobserver agreement of non-parallel transmission technology zoomed-diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for ordinal biparametric Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS)-based scoring in bladder cancer lesions ≥1 cm
pmc-13654155.creator: Dianyu Wang, Zhenming Zhang, Yanjing Wang, Zhijia Wang, Hanyun Zhang, Cancan Cui, Zhao Zhang, Naiming Xue, Mengchao Zhang, Lin Liu
pmc-13654155.description: BackgroundPreoperative assessment of muscle invasion in bladder cancer using the Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) relies heavily on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), but conventional single-shot echo-planar imaging diffusion-weighted imaging (ss-EPI-DWI) may be limited by image distortion and artifacts, potentially affecting interobserver agreement. Zoomed diffusion-weighted imaging without parallel transmission technology (non-pTx zoomed-DWI) may improve image quality.
